analysis.title: Nordic Outlook Update, November 2026: Growth challenged by rising interest rates and high energy prices
key_insights: SEB raises its global GDP forecast by 0.1 percentage points for both 2026 and 2027. World GDP (PPP) is forecast at 3.2% in 2026 and 3.3% in 2027, supported by AI, defence and energy investment, an improving manufacturing cycle and stable labour markets.

High energy prices are driving inflation. Brent is just under USD 100 per barrel and WTI is around USD 90. Brent is up about 40% and European gas (TTF) almost 3x versus levels before the US attacked Iran. Persistent concern about renewed US attacks after the midterms keeps prices elevated.
SEB forecasts one more Fed hike in December 2026, taking the policy rate from 4.00% to 4.25%. The Fed then cuts in the latter part of 2027, with the rate at 4.00% by Dec 2027 and 3.50% by mid-2028.

The ECB is forecast to hike in December 2026 and March 2027, taking the deposit rate from 2.50% to 3.00%. The December hike is seen as fairly certain. The March hike may not happen if energy prices fall faster than expected. Cuts follow in early 2028.

The Riksbank has raised once and signals more. SEB expects one more hike within six months, to a 2.25% policy rate, then a hold through the forecast horizon. Norges Bank is judged to have peaked at 4.50% and is expected to hold before cautious cuts late in 2027 and in 2028.

SEB regards market pricing for the Fed, ECB, Bank of England and Riksbank as somewhat too aggressive. Pricing has eased recently as higher long-term yields tightened financial conditions and energy prices fell.

The Fed left rates unchanged in October, but two members favoured a hike. SEB says the Fed's models and lending surveys show conditions are still accommodative despite higher long-term yields, which supports a little more tightening. Fed Chair Warsh says the aim is to make policy more neutral, not to impede growth.

Long-term yields are expected to move sideways or slightly higher near term, then decline gradually. SEB forecasts the US 10-year at 4.84% on 5 Nov, 5.00% in Dec 2026 and 4.40% in Dec 2028. Structural drivers are large government borrowing, AI, defence and energy investment, and shrinking central bank balance sheets.

France is the main fiscal risk: a deficit of almost 5.5% of GDP, public debt of almost 120% of GDP and a presidential election in April 2027. SEB thinks the French-German spread is still narrower than at past ECB interventions. A much larger rise in French yields, with spillovers, would be needed for the ECB to act.

In the US midterms, Democrats took both chambers of Congress. This forces fiscal negotiation with the Trump administration, while tariffs, immigration and foreign policy stay largely under presidential control. Overriding a veto needs a two-thirds majority in both chambers.

The dollar is expected to stay supported short term by high rates and safe-haven demand, then weaken gradually as US rate cuts are priced in during late 2027 and 2028. The EUR/USD range held for 18 months was broken in October. SEB forecasts EUR/USD at 1.12 now, 1.16 by Jun 2027 and 1.19 by Dec 2028.

The Swedish krona is expected to strengthen significantly in 2027, with EUR/SEK going from 11.00 to 10.55 by Dec 2027. The Norwegian krone is expected to weaken significantly against the krona and the euro in 2027. The yen is expected to remain the weakest major currency.

Global equities were range-bound until last week on AI profitability doubts. A sharp tech sell-off last week pushed the whole market down. Q3 earnings were strong and estimates keep rising. SEB's base case is that AI investment growth slows in 2027 without turning negative, letting tech stabilise.
Anthropic's planned IPO is described as a key near-term test for the AI boom.

SEB forecasts Brent at an annual average of USD 80 per barrel in 2027 and USD 70 in 2028, roughly in line with futures. If the risk premium disappears, oil could fall rapidly as the supply surplus grows.

Risks are tilted to the downside for growth and the upside for inflation. SEB sees a stagflation-like scenario if it underestimates inflation spillovers while markets doubt AI profitability and fiscal policy is constrained. Core inflation is expected to return toward target only in 2028.

sector_views.rationale: SEB expects AI investment growth to slow in 2027 without turning negative, letting tech shares stabilise after the recent sell-off. Doubts about AI profitability are a key risk.
High energy prices benefit oil producers such as the US and the Middle East in the short term. A greater focus on energy security pressures fossil fuel producers over the longer term.

earnings_insights: The Q3 reporting season was strong and earnings estimates have continued rising, per SEB. The report gives no company-level figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: One more Fed hike is expected in December, then cuts from the latter part of 2027.
Hikes in December and March, then cuts from early 2028.
One more hike within six months, then a hold.
Peak is judged to be reached, with cautious cuts from late 2027.
Yields are seen sideways to slightly higher near term, then easing as cuts are priced.

macro_indicators.reading: just under USD 100 per barrel currently; forecast USD 93 average 2026, USD 78 in the table / USD 80 in the text for 2027, USD 70 in 2028
macro_indicators.interpretation: The forecast sits broadly in line with futures. Prices stay high on fears of renewed US attacks on Iran.
Raised by 0.1 percentage point for both years versus August.
Growth is broadening, with AI investment offset by its high import content.
Headline inflation is lifted by energy, with limited pass-through to core.
Headline inflation is expected to fall below target in 2028 if energy declines as expected.
Growth is reasonable but held back by energy prices, France and Chinese competition.

macro_indicators.reading: Budget deficit almost 5.5% of GDP, public debt almost 120% of GDP
macro_indicators.interpretation: The weak fiscal position is widening French-German spreads and weighing on the euro.
Growth is export-led. It drifts toward the lower end of the 4.5-5.0% target range without rebalancing.

risk_factors: Underestimated inflation spillovers combined with doubts about AI profitability could produce a stagflation-like scenario with limited fiscal room.
Renewed US attacks on Iran or damage to production facilities or transport routes could keep energy prices high for longer.
Rising long-term yields threaten the AI investment cycle, housing and equity valuations.
Inflation expectations de-anchoring from central bank targets would change the bond outlook.
French fiscal stress and political crisis could spill over to other countries and banks.
Chinese low-cost AI competition and calls from US Democrats for temporary pauses in AI expansion are concerns for AI companies.
Weak consumer confidence, a low US savings ratio and slower wage growth limit consumption upside.
vol_and_positioning: Global stocks were range-bound until a sharp tech sell-off last week pushed the whole market down. The report gives no VIX or options data.
Market pricing of central bank policy has fluctuated sharply with energy prices over the summer and autumn, and has eased recently.
geopolitical: The US attacked Iran, and the war continues. SEB cites the risk of renewed US attacks after the midterm elections as the reason energy prices stay high.
Escalating Russian hybrid attacks and the ongoing war in Ukraine strain Europe's security situation.
US-China trade and technology wars continue. The EU is seeking to restrict imports of Chinese products in selected sectors.
Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the US midterms. They may join some Republicans to halt the war with Iran or increase Ukraine support.
Protest movements are growing in France, Italy, Serbia, India and Indonesia against high living costs, AI labour disruption, corruption and government cutbacks.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment growth slows in 2027 without turning negative, letting tech stabilise. Q3 earnings were strong and estimates keep rising. Lower oil and easing rate pressure support the broader market.
tension_points.bear_case: Doubts about AI companies' business models and profitability, Chinese low-cost AI competition, calls for pauses in AI expansion and rising rates have unsettled stock markets. A sharp tech sell-off last week pushed the whole market down.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Anthropic's planned IPO is called a key near-term test for the AI boom.

tension_points.bull_case: Indirect effects remain limited, wage growth is slowing, long-term inflation expectations are stable, and core inflation returns toward 2% in 2028, allowing cuts in 2027-2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Repeated cost shocks from tariffs and energy could create second-round effects and push inflation higher. Central banks would then have to tighten more.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation expectations becoming de-anchored from central bank targets would change the bond market outlook.

theme_stances.key_argument: High energy prices drive inflation, which leads the Fed, ECB and Riksbank to hike once or twice more before cutting later.
theme_stances.evidence: Inflation concerns will prompt central banks, including the ECB, the Fed and the Riksbank, to further hike
